summary.oneLiner: and, critically, putting a hard floor under future credit losses. Management reiterates full-year guidance of 19, 23, and framed the JHL/JCL promoter rating "technical default" as a ring-fenced non-event with no linkage to the bank.

one-line thesis: The MFI stress is decisively behind Jana: Q1FY27 PAT Rs 155 cr (vs Rs 140 cr in Q4), NIM restored to 7.5%, credit cost flat at 0.45%, and — critically — the historically brutal first quarter came out clean. The structural de-risking is the story: the bank is travelling toward an 80% secured book while simultaneously ~80% of its unsecured (MFI) book sits under a CGMFU guarantee program (Rs 196 cr of the Rs 214 cr unsecured net NPA covered), putting a hard floor under future credit losses. Management reiterates full-year guidance of 19–21% loan growth, 23–25% deposit growth and 80%+ PAT growth, and framed the JHL/JCL promoter rating "technical default" as a ring-fenced non-event with no linkage to the bank.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy): > Segment books: Gold Rs 2,678 cr (+13.5% QoQ, +100% YoY, LTV 64%); MFI Rs 10,240 cr (+2.8% QoQ, +18% YoY, ~27% of total book); Used Car ~Rs 45 cr/month disbursement (launched Oct-2025, in ~50 cities). Unsecured slippages fell ~20% QoQ (Rs 155 cr → Rs 125 cr). Capital raise: total Rs 728 cr; first Rs 103 cr received, next ~Rs 80 cr on TVS RBI approval, balance 75% over 18 months.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: Gross loan growth: 19–21% for FY27 (achievable from own product lines alone; NBFC term-loan book deliberately flat).
Deposit growth: 23–25% for FY27.
PAT growth: 80%+ for FY27 (after absorbing Rs 80–100 cr guarantee-commission cost).
NIM: steady ~7.5%.
Cost of funds: plateau ~7.3–7.4% (±5 bps); further cuts "over".
Credit cost: 0.45% at minimum maintained across all remaining quarters.
Cost-to-income: reduce to 63–65% during the year (won't go below 60%).
CASA ratio: target ~20% for the year.
MFI growth: deliberately modest 10–12% YoY (not aggressive).
Secured mix: continue toward 80% every year (from 72.8%).
CGMFU recovery: claim Rs 65 cr in Q3 (first-ever guarantee recoveries).
Product launches (Q2): Credit Line on UPI goes public; Loans Against Shares (RBI-approved Rs 1 cr limit). Nostro/trade-FX setup this month; possible small FCNR(B) in Aug/Sep.
Branches: 78 planned (8 new, 30 split, 40 relocations — only 7 executed); +50–75 gold-capable branches over next 2 quarters.
order book & pipeline: Not applicable (bank). Forward pipeline = product + distribution build-out: Credit Line on UPI (mass-scale, small-ticket) and Loans Against Shares both live Q2; used-car finance scaling from 50 → up to 240 cities (matching affordable-housing/Micro-LAP footprint); TVS Motors strategic tie-up expected to aid two-wheeler and vehicle-finance growth. Anchor-bank cross-sell at 3.9 active products/customer (Gold penetration 3%, up from 2%; Two-Wheeler 1.1%).
segment / subsidiary detail: Gold loans: Rs 2,678 cr, +100% YoY / +13.5% QoQ; LTV 64%, daily price feeds + margin-call mechanism; GNPA ~0.5% fully collateral-covered; adding gold headcount + 50–75 gold branches. Unfazed by recent gold-price correction.
MFI (unsecured): Rs 10,240 cr, +18% YoY; 5 consecutive quarters of declining slippages; ~80% under CGMFU guarantee; targeted growth only 10–12% FY27 — stabilizing, not chasing.
Micro LAP: the one deliberate Q1 "blip" — model shifting to direct sourcing (from DSA); returns to positive growth Q2.
NBFC term loans: deliberately reduced/flat — own products strong enough to hit 20–22% growth without it.
Affordable housing / MSME(MSE) / Two-Wheeler: all growing well; MSE flagged for a strong Q2 acceleration; affordable housing may accelerate.
Liabilities: CASA +31% YoY (7.1% QoQ, RCB/IPL branding aided); retail TD +31% YoY; bulk cut 6% QoQ to lower cost of funds; 97% retail & 83% bulk deposits are 1-year+.
growth verticals / optionality: Credit Line on UPI — mass-scale small-ticket lending (consumer durables, education, medical emergencies); management has "a lot of expectations."
Loans Against Shares — new wealth-management offering (RBI Rs 1 cr limit).
Used-car finance — 50 → 240-city runway; currently no BT/refinance program (pure buy/sell financing) = large untapped optionality.
Trade FX / FCNR(B) / Nostro — building non-resident + trade franchise.
TVS Motors strategic partnership — potential two-wheeler / vehicle-finance flywheel once RBI approves.
6a. moat & competitive position (optiona: Guarantee-program floor on unsecured losses: since Nov-2024 the bank pre-emptively placed ~80% of MFI under a CGMFU guarantee — Rs 196 cr of the Rs 214 cr unsecured net NPA is covered (uncovered only Rs 18 cr). This structurally caps the tail risk that historically caused every misstep (MFI/COVID). Management calls a fully-covered unsecured book + secured majority "nearly a secured bank."

Diversified secured franchise: five secured product lines (affordable housing, Micro LAP, MSME, vehicle, gold) vs a single unsecured line mathematically pushes the mix toward 80% secured each year — a self-reinforcing de-risking.
margins & cost dynamics: NIM 7.5%, restored to pre-MFI-stress levels via (1) cost-of-funds decline (−60 bps YoY to 7.4%) and (2) lower slippage → reduced interest-in-suspense. Cost of funds is now near its floor (7.3–7.4% range) as deposit pricing hardened in April–May and the bank raised rates in June. Operating leverage is the next lever: opex grew only Rs 10 cr (+1.6%) QoQ against ~20% asset growth, targeting cost-to-income down to 63–65%. Note the ~Rs 80–100 cr annual guarantee-commission (1%) is now a permanent BAU cost — absorbed while still guiding 80%+ PAT growth.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Branch program: 78 actions planned (8 new, 30 splits, 40 relocations) — only 7 executed so far (watch pace); +50–75 gold-capable branches over the next 2 quarters (current ~568–570 gold branches of 820 total). Product build-out (Credit Line on UPI, LAS, Nostro) is largely opex/systems, not heavy capex.
capital allocation: Capital raise total Rs 728 cr: Rs 103 cr received, ~Rs 80 cr pending TVS RBI approval, balance 75% staged over 18 months. Promoters (JHL/JCL) have not funded the bank since June-2022 (diluting from 44% → 16.9%); bank self-funds via IPO/private investors. Guarantee commission (Rs 80–100 cr/yr) is a deliberate capital-protection spend. No buyback/dividend detail.
risks & watch-items: Promoter (JHL/JCL) "technical default": India Ratings downgraded the holdcos after NCD holders sought a 6-month extension to sell shares. Management stresses: no cross-default, no common board members, no bank liability, CARE did not put the bank on watch. Reputational/overhang risk, not a financial one — but monitor.
Deposit pricing / liquidity: April–May were tight; rates raised in June; total deposits flat QoQ — deposit growth must re-accelerate to hit 23–25% guidance (H1 catch-up needed).
MFI concentration: ~27% of book; slippages improving but Q2 slippage guided flattish (with better recoveries offsetting).
Government CASA: state-government deposits lost in Q4 not yet returned (bank re-empaneled; flow "started marginally," pace uncertain).
Macro: Iran war / El Nino — no impact seen yet; monitored via early-warning indicators.
Merger speculation in media — management declined to comment.
CGMFU claim timing: Rs 65 cr claimed Q3, balance later — recovery is a timing question, not a coverage question.
management quality / tone: Confident, granular and unusually direct. Ajay Kanwal proactively (and at length) addressed the promoter rating downgrade "in such an obvious manner" rather than dodging, and volunteered spreadsheet-relevant nuances (Q2 slippage flattish but recoveries improving). CFO Sandur gave precise segment numbers on demand; ED Raman handled gold and macro-risk crisply. Candid on the deposit-side "work to do" in Q2 and honest on government-deposit uncertainty ("tough to predict"). Tone: post-crisis relief + measured optimism ("best year ever"), backed by data rather than hype.
non-obvious takeaways: The guarantee program is the real re-rating catalyst, not the PAT — with ~80% of unsecured covered and the book heading to 80% secured, Jana is engineering away the exact tail risk (unsecured blow-ups) that caused every prior misstep. The Rs 80–100 cr commission is the "insurance premium" for earnings predictability.
The clean Q1 matters more than the absolute number — management repeatedly flagged that Q1 is seasonally "a shocker" and last year's Q1 was brutal; a strong Q1 de-risks the full-year guidance.
Cost-of-funds tailwind is exhausted — future NIM defense shifts to asset-mix (higher-yield gold, secured retail) and operating leverage, not cheaper liabilities.
NBFC-lending pullback is a quality signal — the bank is confident enough in its own 5 product lines to shrink wholesale NBFC exposure and still hit 20%+ growth.
Micro LAP negative growth is self-inflicted and temporary (DSA→direct sourcing transition), not credit stress — an important distinction for anyone modeling the book.
